projectstore · 0.30.0 · project memory for coding agents, in markdown

Usage
  npx projectstore <verb> [options]  run it inside your code project
  npx projectstore <verb> --help     one verb's options and examples

START
  install      Install projectstore's surfaces for a harness, behind a preview.
  bind         Bind this project to an existing vault; naming it confirms.
  uninstall    Remove what install wrote, and only that.

VAULT
  status       What is bound, what is in progress, and whether views are fresh.
  search       Find a phrase in the vault's artifacts, literal and bounded.
  show         One artifact's frontmatter; its body or a section on request.
  graph        The live link graph by vault path.
  codemap      The code an epic or artifact maps to, or a path's artifacts.

CHECK AND REPAIR
  doctor       Check the install wiring and the vault's consistency.
  reconcile    Regenerate the derived views (kanban, code map, graph, indexes).
  upgrade      After an update, refresh what install wrote and leave the rest.

ADVANCED
  plan · orientation · agents · init · scaffold · mcp · version

Options
  --project <dir>  the project (default: the session's, else this directory)
  --json           the result as one JSON envelope, for scripts and agents
  --version        the package version

Examples

  npx projectstore install --harness <id>
  npx projectstore status
  npx projectstore doctor

Tips
  install, upgrade and uninstall show their plan, then ask at a terminal.
  Without a terminal, --harness is the confirmation — there is no --yes.
  Unattended in a terminal: pass --json, set CI=1, or give stdin </dev/null.
  --verbose on those verbs adds every row's reasoning and the host's notes.
  plan prints the same plan and writes nothing:

  npx projectstore plan --harness <id>

Harnesses   claude-code, codex
Exit codes  0 ok, 1 findings or a refusal, 2 usage, 3 not bound, 130 cancelled
